checks.detail: kernel enters at the hourly close; the live bot scans every 5 min on a forming candle, so the kernel reads pumps +0.59pp larger on average (200 matched setups). DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: entry-8pct and vol-4x both report screen_dWR=0.0pp, i.e. no win-rate effect versus control.
findings.problem: Those two arms report screen_wr=51.613 and screen_wr=51.27 against control's screen_wr=49.935 on the same screen — non-zero differences that are being displayed as an exact 0.0pp delta. The same 0.0pp appears for placebo, where it is genuinely zero. So the field is not a delta at all for the two arms whose screen_n (496 and 866) differs from control's 1550; it is a default that renders 'not computed' as 'no effect'. Every other arm with screen_n=1550 has a real delta (tp-7pct -3.42pp, hold-12h 3.23pp), which is exactly the pattern of a delta that silently zeroes out when the populations do not match.

findings.claim: 'measured ghost arrival = 25.2 control trades/day', used to size the planned confirm n=600.
findings.problem: That rate is a backfill/screen quantity, not a live-tape one: control's screen_n is 1550 over a 62.0-day data span, which is where ~25/day comes from. The live tier holds only 50 events in total, and control's live record is live_n=13 with declined=33 and 4 still open — 50 events, not 25 per day. Meanwhile backfill_cannot_promote is green precisely because only live-tape evidence may promote. Sizing the promotion timeline off the backfill arrival rate imports backfill into the one decision it is barred from, and makes n=600 look reachable in weeks when the live tape shows 13 resolved control trades.

findings.claim: Checklist item paired_population, critical=true, titled 'Every arm scored on identical events'.
findings.problem: The supporting detail establishes something weaker than the title: that all 4814 events were *seen* by every arm. Scoring is not identical. entry-8pct is scored on screen_n=496 and vol-4x on screen_n=866 against control's 1550, because filter arms decline events. Their reported screen_wr therefore describes a self-selected subpopulation, and any comparison against control's screen_wr is unpaired — unlike the retired sl-entry-anchor kill, which could quote a genuine paired test (b=0/c=134 on n=1474). A green critical check whose title asserts paired scoring, resting on a detail that only shows shared detection, is a checkbox green for a reason that does not establish it.

findings.claim: Checklist item no_lookahead, critical=true: 'Detection is look-ahead free'.
findings.problem: The evidence is a re-detection of 108 events across 6 coins. The shared window holds 4814 events across 176 coins, so this probe covers roughly two percent of events and six of 176 coins, and no coin-selection rule is stated. Given that this project's single largest documented failure class is look-ahead (G-01, G-18, and the methodology line 'any look-ahead number is disqualified'), a clean result on a 6-coin sample does not license a green critical check for the detector as a whole. Note the kernel_agreement misses cluster in one name — four of five are BOME — which is what a coin-specific detection issue would look like.

findings.claim: Checklist item graveyard_enforced: 'Dead ideas are refused automatically', verified because a probe naming 'peak-close' was refused by G-01.
findings.problem: The probe only demonstrates that an exact blocked term matches its own blocklist entry — a positive control on the string, not on the reasoning. The kill records show the cost of that: dedup-0h and dedup-48h are opposite interventions (remove deduplication entirely versus extend it to two days) and were both refused as 'REFUTED_BEFORE: matches G-06 via cascade'. One keyword cannot have refuted two interventions pointing in opposite directions. All four dedup arms and minprice-1 now sit at screen_n=0 — retired without ever being measured — so the graveyard is producing kills that carry no evidence behind them, while the checkbox reports this as working correctly.

findings.claim: 'MECHANISM CLASSES (one per running arm — diversity is enforced in code)'.
findings.problem: The running arms do not satisfy this. entry_trigger is held by both control (changed={}) and entry-8pct; liquidity_filter is held by both placebo (min_price=1e-12) and vol-4x. Two of six declared classes are doubled among the seven running arms. Either the constraint is not enforced for the control and placebo baselines — in which case the stated rule is wrong as written and baselines are consuming class slots that a real arm could use — or enforcement is not happening. Since arms_running reports '5 running' while the arena lists seven arms in running/confirm state, the code and the display already disagree on what counts as a running arm.
